key_insight: A forensic audit found that multiple benchmark artifacts did not match the intended protocol, so the paper withdraws its original performance and prompt-effect claims.
clinical_relevance: This matters because radiology AI conclusions can be invalid if dataset handling, DICOM rendering, prompts, and analysis code are not fully consistent and traceable.
method: Retrospective audit of a preserved chest-radiograph vision-language model benchmark
Checked prompt bindings, DICOM metadata, output completeness, label extraction, matched analyses, and release artifacts
Reconstructed one complete-case cohort and compared archived statistical results
evidence_signal: Of 300 planned model calls, 297 returned reports; the audit also found 4 MONOCHROME1 images rendered without polarity inversion and 5 reports truncated to 4000 characters.
watch_item: The findings apply to the archived automated-label matrix only and do not establish clinical performance or the intended prompt comparison.
paper_title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology Vision-Language Model Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact
